question: Does the UPLB repository record provide new, independently usable river-and-species evidence beyond the published Bataan river studies?

officialRepositoryRecord.title: River health assessment using the fish-based index of biotic integrity and socio-ecological system assessment in selected river systems in Bataan, Philippines
officialRepositoryRecord.author: Mark Nell Castillo Corpuz
officialRepositoryRecord.degree: Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Science
officialRepositoryRecord.repositoryAccessStatement: The item page says the document is currently not available there.
officialRepositoryRecord.repositoryListedHolding: UPLB Main Library Special Collections Section (USCS)
officialRepositoryRecord.itemSpecificReuseTerms: Not stated on the reviewed repository item page; no reuse permission inferred.

abstractReportedStudyScope.interpretation: These are abstract-level claims for a dissertation spanning four unnamed Bataan river systems. They are not a taxon list, river-by-river allocation, voucher crosswalk, or current occurrence inventory.

2025ThreeRiverPaper.relationship: The dissertation and paper share the lead author and the repository lists several paper co-authors on the dissertation committee. The accessible dissertation record does not name its four rivers or give sampling dates, so the three-river overlap and relationship between the reported totals cannot be determined.

relationshipToPublishedBataanStudies.decision: Keep dissertation aggregate claims separate from every published survey. The difference in counts does not establish a new species, a fourth named river, independent samples, or an error; a full-text site/date/taxon/method and specimen crosswalk is needed.

evidenceDisposition.decision: Metadata-only access and research-lineage lead. Do not infer river identities, extract species from the abstract aggregate, or treat the thesis as independent confirmation of the 2025 paper.

nextActions: If this source is needed for the Bataan coverage baseline, ask UPLB Main Library Special Collections about legitimate consultation or access and any reproduction conditions; no request was sent in this review.

If the full text becomes available, independently review river names, sampling dates/seasons, species tables, station and voucher identifiers, methods, and any crosswalk to Corpuz et al. (2025) before adding source-scoped findings.
Keep Central Luzon and Luzon marked incomplete until the regional habitat and waterbody baselines are reconciled.

sources.supports: Official UPLB repository citation, author, date, dissertation type/degree, abstract-level scope and counts, listed library holding, and statement that the document is not available there.
Separate published three-river survey scope and figures as already transcribed in the existing source review; this comparison does not establish shared or independent specimens.
